source.title: Towards Generating Informative Textual Description for Neurons in Language Models
source.authors: Shrayani Mondal; Rishabh Garodia; Arbaaz Qureshi; Taesung Lee; Youngja Park

record.tranche_reason: The study varies descriptor assignment and scoring choices for neuron explanations, providing evidence about measurement sensitivity, but does not use the original vision-neuron method.
record.gate_note: The study measures BERT neuron descriptors and reports how descriptor scores and consistency vary with composition threshold and top-K scoring. It does not report how many neurons respond to unrelated inputs or the prevalence of polysemantic neurons. Results about sentence-level descriptor annotation and cited findings from other work are not rows.
record.test_reason: This is a neuron-description method paper on BERT [CLS] activations. Every row reports the method's own performance: precision and recall against ChatGPT labels, and calibration/validation Jaccard consistency, each as a function of its threshold t or K. It allows several descriptors per neuron, but never asks whether these are unrelated. It reports no share of polysemantic neurons and never uses the term. Threshold sensitivity is a property of its scoring pipeline, not evidence about when a neuron counts as polysemantic, so V7 is not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that their unsupervised LLM-based framework yields useful, data-specific neuron descriptors (75% precision@2, 50% recall@2 on 10 BERT neurons). They also report that the descriptors are consistent across disjoint calibration and validation splits (Jaccard 0.95 at t=0.35), suggesting they are not spurious.
record.recipe_differences: Uses generated text descriptors, sentence labels, and top-activating BERT review sentences; it does not reproduce the original vision-neuron method.
record.method_sensitivity: Descriptor precision and neuron-set consistency vary with composition threshold; precision@K peaks at K=2.

fits_no_version.finding: Neurons are tagged with sets of descriptors, and the size of the set shrinks as the composition threshold rises (Sections 5.1 and 5.3). Three broad descriptors (Positive, Product Quality, User Experience) had high activation for over 80% of neurons and were discarded. Relatedness between descriptors is not assessed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: How many concepts a BERT neuron is assigned under frequency-threshold descriptor tagging depends on the threshold, and broad sentiment/quality descriptors dominate most neurons' top-activating sentences.

record.code_released: not stated; the authors say they plan to open-source the code with a camera-ready version if accepted.
record.problems: The quantitative neuron-descriptor evaluation uses 10 randomly selected neurons. The experiments use one discriminative model and one review dataset; the authors note that evaluation on other models and datasets, and on generative models, is left for future work. Standard deviations are shown in plots but exact uncertainty values are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported neuron-level polysemanticity counts or results about neurons responding to unrelated inputs. Sentence-label annotation results are not neuron-behavior measurements.

untested.parts: All; BERT neurons are described, but there is no share of neurons responding to unrelated contexts and no layer comparison.
All; no architecture, activation-function or regularization comparison.
All; whether multiple descriptors per neuron are related is not analysed.
There is no polysemanticity classification whose dependence on activation range or scoring could be measured. Threshold effects concern the method's own descriptor-assignment accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: The paper does not mention polysemanticity or superposition. The record's V7 'tested' status and its 'supports' label conflate sensitivity of the method's evaluation to its own hyperparameters with measurement-dependence of polysemanticity classification. Evaluation covers only 10 neurons, with ChatGPT used as a proxy for ground truth.

versions.untested_parts: The study uses BERT, but does not report the share of neurons responding to unrelated tokens or contexts, or compare such a share across layers.
Does not test superposition or capacity pressure as a cause of polysemanticity.
Does not test initialization, regularization, training noise, or whether capacity is sufficient for each feature.
Does not compare architectures, activation functions, regularization, or performance costs.
Does not investigate whether apparently unrelated neuron responses share a feature.
Varies descriptor composition threshold and top-K scoring, but not the portion of the activation range examined; it does not directly measure the number of neurons classified as polysemantic.

rows.subject: BERT-base-uncased

rows.operation_detail: Measured precision of neuron descriptors while varying composition threshold.
rows.value: The text reports a general increase in precision as the composition threshold increases; exact values are figure only.
rows.uncertainty: Standard deviation shown in Figure 5; exact values not stated.
rows.note: Shows sensitivity of descriptor scoring to the composition threshold; the paper does not translate this into a count of polysemantic neurons.
rows.check: This is the method's precision against LLM-derived ground truth as threshold varies. It is own-method performance, not a measure of polysemanticity. Values are figure-only.

rows.operation_detail: Compared neuron descriptor sets from calibration and validation subsets using Jaccard similarity while varying composition threshold.
rows.measure: Average neuron-level Jaccard similarity of descriptor sets
rows.value: 0.95 at composition threshold 0.35; similarity drops when the threshold is increased beyond 0.35.
rows.uncertainty: Standard deviation shown in Figure 6; exact value not stated.
rows.note: The text also describes increasing the threshold from 0.05 to 0.35 as removing low-frequency descriptors.
rows.check: This is the consistency of descriptor sets across data splits (Jaccard 0.95 at t=0.35). It is a stability score for the method, not a rate of polysemantic neurons.

reader_labels.reason: Descriptor precision and calibration/validation similarity vary with composition threshold, and precision@K peaks at K=2; these results show that explanation measurements depend on scoring choices (r1–r5).
